title: Grateful Dead Live at Pirates World on 1970-03-24
lineage: SBD > MR > Cass > DAT > Cass > DAT > ZA2 > CD Wave > SHN

ai_review.summary: Clean soundboard recording with an odd instrument‑vs‑vocal panning captures a stellar early‑70 set highlighted by Dark Star, Good Lovin', High Time and seamless segues.
ai_review.review: The show is praised as a prime example of the Dead in 1970, featuring inspired performances of Dark Star, Good Lovin', High Time, The Other One, St. Stephen, NFA, Lovelight and Me & My Uncle. Reviewers note Jerry’s soulful guitar work, Bob Weir’s standout rhythm/vocals and jazzy drumming, while the soundboard is generally clean despite a quirky stereo mix that puts most instruments on one side and vocals on the other.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high reviewer scores (average ~4.3) and strong positive language about both performance and sound quality, with only minor mix quirks mentioned.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clean overall sound but unusual stereo separation (most instruments on one channel, vocals on the other). Opening Dew is cut short; otherwise no major drop‑outs or muddiness.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set is praised for inventive segues—High Time → Dark Star → The Other One → St. Stephen → Drums → NFA → Lovelight → Me and My Uncle—creating a flowing, exploratory journey.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar tone and soulful playing are highlighted, especially on High Time and the expansive Dark Star jam.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir receives high praise for his rhythm guitar work and vocal delivery, notably on the Good Lovin' jam and a beautiful Cold Rain & Snow.
band_member_comments.Drums: Jazzy, creative drumming is noted in the jam into Good Lovin' and the transition to NFA.
